The "Main Gate Syndrome," also referred to as "The Main Gate Syndrome," is a novel concept in mass-casualty victim "surge" management. This approach involves setting up an additional, semi-evacuation hospital or receiving center near the scene of the incident, specifically designed to handle and manage patients who require immediate medical attention due to overcrowding at the primary evacuation hospital.

The idea behind this strategy is to provide a second line of care for patients who are being overwhelmed by the volume of casualties at the existing evacuation hospital. This approach allows surgeons and anesthetists to share expertise, opinions, and experiences, leading to improved outcomes in managing mass casualty situations.

In essence, The Main Gate Syndrome aims to mitigate the risks associated with overcrowding at the primary evacuation hospital and ensure that patients receive timely and effective medical care, even in the most chaotic of situations.
